messages:
jessica.m: quick summary of cross-cloud sku run — ran the same model (redwood-llama-13b quantized w/ q4_0) across AWS (p4d / A100 40GB), GCP (a2-highgpu / A100 40GB), and Azure (ND96asr / A100 40GB) with identical CUDA 11.8 + driver 525.85.12 and same container image. Results are... mixed.

riley: curious — mixed how? numbers please :eyes:

jessica.m: p50 similar across all (around 70–85 ms for single-token step at bs=1), but p99 diverges: AWS p99=220ms, GCP p99=170ms, Azure p99=280ms. throughput (tokens/sec) at bs=8: AWS 8.1k, GCP 9.4k, Azure 6.7k.

devon: wow Azure lagging. same PCIe gen / topology? could be NVLink config or driver kernel build.

arjun: i dug into kernel selection: our runtime auto-picked cuBLAS/TF-like fused-kernel path on GCP, but fell back to more generic kernels on Azure because of different nvlink topology + mem stride assumptions. that explains throughput drop.

maya: any differences in CPU affinity / cgroup settings on the VMs? we saw host config affect pipelining in previous tests.

jessica.m: good question — we pinned cpus the same. found an extra NUMA node on Azure image, the instance had asymmetric NUMA mapping (2 GPUs on one socket, 2 on another) and our allocator wasn't NUMA-aware so a lot of KV cache allocations crossed nodes.

infra-bot: nightly-bench finished: job/1767854001 on gcp returned 0. (!). Attached logs to run: gs://redwood-bench/gcp/1767854001/log.txt

riley: did we use the same MIG / instance partitioning? that will change context-switch cost.

jessica.m: no MIG used — full A100. single process per GPU. also tested with int8 (tensorRT) path: GCP gains ~12% tokens/sec but small BLEU-like metric drop (~0.7 pts) on our eval prompts; AWS int8 wins latency but introduced hallucination pattern increase on slot-filling tests.

devon: that's concerning — quantization kernel differences can change ordering of fused matmuls, rounding noise. we should gate int8 on model-specific eval suite.

arjun: agreed. proposed action: 1) add NUMA-aware allocator/affinity to runtime (short term fix), 2) extend eval harness to include the production prompt set (to catch quant regressions), 3) rerun on Azure with our patched allocator.

maya: also try building drivers with CONFIG_PCI_BARS or different IB switch MTU? previous Azure runs improved when we forced nvlink bonding on similar SKUs.

jessica.m: i'll open a small PR for the allocator change and queue bench reruns. command used for runs:```bash
python infra/bench/run.py --model redwood-llama-13b --quant q4_0 --bs 8 --seq 1024 --backend cutorch --repeat 600
# env: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0; export TF_NEED_CUDA=0
```

riley: can you also paste nvidia-smi/topology dumps? helps infra validate hardware differences.

jessica.m: pasted snippets below:```
# aws node topology (nvlink present between 0-1, 2-3)
NVLINK: 0<->1 1<->0 2<->3 3<->2
# azure node: topology reported with weaker links, some PCIe fallback between 1-2
NVLINK: 0<->1 2<->3 (1<->2 via PCIe bridge)
```

ci-bot: perf/regression job queued: perf/1767854500 (target: azure, patch: allocator-numa-fix).

devon: ok plan sounds good. also add a simple microbench for fused-kernel latency to detect kernel fallback early in onboarding flow.

jessica.m: noted. I'll track in the onboarding checklist and include region-specific kernel hints in the model card. tagging @eng-infra for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
